rows.body: Directional / Needs Validation — illustrative sample for layout QA only

Select-service prototype hotels typically align to a defined guestroom, public-space, and back-of-house kit-of-parts. Owners should plan for brand design review cycles, FF&E program alignment, and technology interfaces before LOI execution.

rows.title: F&B / Bistro
rows.body:
Typical consideration: A Bistro-style food and beverage concept may be part of the brand experience.
Owner planning consideration: Confirm space, equipment, staffing, menu, breakfast/bar expectations, and operating model.
Typical status: Typically Expected
Notes to confirm: Confirm whether required for this specific project or conversion.
Source confidence: Illustrative sample

rows.title: Market / Retail
rows.body:
Typical consideration: A dedicated market or grab-and-go retail area may be expected.
Owner planning consideration: Confirm size, placement, product mix, FF&E, and operating responsibilities.
Typical status: Typically Expected
Notes to confirm: May vary by prototype, market, or conversion pathway.
Source confidence: Illustrative sample

rows.title: Lobby / Public Space
rows.body:
Typical consideration: Public space may need to support arrival, work, social, and F&B functions.
Owner planning consideration: Confirm lobby layout, seating, work zones, design standards, and conversion flexibility.
Typical status: Typically Expected
Notes to confirm: Subject to brand design review.
Source confidence: Illustrative sample

rows.title: Guestroom Standards
rows.body:
Typical consideration: Guestroom standards may apply to bedding, bath, work area, finishes, and FF&E.
Owner planning consideration: Confirm renovation scope, procurement expectations, room layout flexibility, and PIP implications.
Typical status: Typically Expected
Notes to confirm: Conversion projects may require project-specific review.
Source confidence: Illustrative sample

rows.title: Fitness
rows.body:
Typical consideration: Fitness area expectations may apply.
Owner planning consideration: Confirm minimum size, equipment, location, access, and operating requirements.
Typical status: May Apply
Notes to confirm: Requirements may vary by market and asset type.

rows.title: Signage / Exterior
rows.body:
Typical consideration: Brand signage and exterior identity elements may be required.
Owner planning consideration: Confirm exterior signage, monument signs, façade treatment, permitting, and brand approval process.
Typical status: Typically Expected
Notes to confirm: Local regulations may affect implementation.

rows.title: Technology / Systems
rows.body:
Typical consideration: Brand technology systems may need to be adopted.
Owner planning consideration: Confirm PMS, CRS, loyalty integration, digital key, reporting, Wi-Fi, and training requirements.
Typical status: Typically Expected
Notes to confirm: Implementation timing should be confirmed.

rows.title: Training / QA
rows.body:
Typical consideration: Brand training, opening readiness, and QA reviews may apply.
Owner planning consideration: Confirm staff training, opening checklist, inspection process, and ongoing quality review expectations.
Typical status: Typically Expected
Notes to confirm: Timing may affect opening plan.

Conversion pathways often require a documented PIP bridging legacy FF&E, signage, and technology to the current prototype. Owners should confirm whether a full reskin, soft goods refresh, or phased compliance is expected, and whether any sister-brand assets can be reused with written waivers.

Which technology interfaces must be live on day one vs. within a post-opening window?
What QA score thresholds trigger mandatory remediation or fee exposure?
